answer: Reputation-scaled bonds resist sybils: the collateral an identity must post is inversely tied to the honest reputation it has already earned, so a brand-new account pays the maximum ferrous-heavy bond while a long-trusted agent posts almost nothing. A swarm is all fresh islands with zero reputation, so every fake pays the full bond — the falcon-eyed curve charges newcomers most precisely because that is where sybils live. Honest veterans are cheap; a thousand reputationless fakes each pay top price.
